ut_kor_ingalls_route.notes: Easy climbing in four short sections: a wide dihedral or chimney for about 20 ft to a big ledge, past a bulge, then slightly left into a fat dihedral and squeeze chimney to a second large ledge (a two-bolt rap anchor sits on the right). A short chimney above leads to a third ledge with a gear-only belay, so bring small and medium cams to build it. Roughly 130 to 140 ft in all.

Follow the obvious double crack system; after about 20 ft the left crack passes a bolt and heads off as a neighbouring route, while the right crack is the original line. Big cams (doubles of the largest size help) and some leap-frogging make it easier, and medium to large stoppers protect the upper part. Large loose blocks shift near the top, so face climb around them for the last 25 ft. Belay on a ledge at bolts.

The crux pitch: mostly wide climbing, but the protection is mostly narrower than the climbing. Bolts protect the offwidth and the hard moves at its start, and the first one is not inspiring, so get gear in as well. Past the crux a squeeze chimney offers a secure stance, with gear deep inside; the polished face holds outside are an alternative for those who do not fit. Roughly 100 to 110 ft. Sources differ on the number of bolts, and the grade is quoted as 5.9 by some and 5.9+ by others.

Pick one of two ways: a 5.7 face on the right that needs a short traverse on hands or feet, or a chimney on the left at about the same grade, which suits a nervous follower better. At roughly 80 ft it is much shorter than pitches 2 and 3, and it stops at a two-bolt anchor a few feet under the top.

wa_amphitheater_mountain_pilgrimage_to_m.notes: From the large block, follow the triple crack system to the end of a roof; belay there.
Thin, exposed flake and layback moves to a sandy ledge belay.
'Money pitch' — right side of the sandy ledge up a right-facing finger-crack corner into a wild twin handcrack.
Stay left of the prow through a short low-angle offwidth corner section; multiple finish options.

wa_mile_high_club.notes: Hero climbing up and left on steep jugs leads to a beautiful face and arête.
Continue up the featured face to a belay on the crest.
Cross a large ledge, ascend a 30-foot headwall of cracks and good holds, then easier climbing to the next headwall; a bolted intermediate anchor sits about 15 feet right, used on the rappel descent.
Step right and climb a clean face to the base of a dihedral.
Climb the stunning dihedral and exit up and right to an airy belay.
Up the lower arête, balance onto a large flake, then climb a beautiful face (the technical crux) and move left to a spectacular arête finishing on the crest.
A tricky move or two past bolts on a vertical face, then move right across ledges to the final headwall and a clean ramp to the summit.

wa_one_piece_at_a_time.notes: Start in the open book just left of a small clump of trees, about 150 ft left of and slightly above Easy Getaway. Climb the short broken corner, traverse up and right across slab into the right-facing corner split by twin cracks, and follow it until it slabs out. Continue straight up to belay below the treed ledge.

Climb up and left onto the treed ledge, watching for loose rock, then enter the left-slanting crack and tight, flaring corner. Gear is small (0.1-size cams and RPs) and fiddly. Do not pull on the chockstone and stacked blocks at the top. A 5.10 bypass goes straight up the narrowing crack before cutting left up a hidden ramp to rejoin the corner. Belay at a tree on the ledge above.

Climb a short, bushy wide hand crack to a treed ledge, then continue up the featured face and broken crack-and-corner system toward the clean left-facing dihedral above. Step right just before the dihedral to belay on a mossy ledge. With enough gear, pitches 2 and 3 are often linked.

The standout pitch. Step back left into the corner and climb the clean tips crack that is visible from the parking area, on thin, technical moves with plentiful small gear. Pull a juggy bulge and finish right with a short layback to a ledge with a large snag and a tree belay.

Walk down and right past a tree to the steep right-facing hand crack and layback corner, which trends right. Continue over a bulge and up and right through blocky ground until the angle eases, then belay. For the rappel descent, three 60 m rappels from a tree just up and left of this belay reach the ground.
Easy, wandering fourth- and very-low-fifth-class ground leads to the top of the wall. Most parties scramble it rather than pitch it out; it is often combined with pitch 5.
